title: GSK delivers strong Q3 performance and continued momentum
body_markdown:
28 October 2026


For media and investors only


Issued: London, UK


# GSK delivers strong Q3 performance and continued momentum


[Download (PDF - 895.3KB)](https://www.gsk.com/media/nw0az1nj/q3-2026-results-announcement.pdf)


Q3 Results 2026


[Q3 2026 results announcement (PDF - 895.3KB)](https://www.gsk.com/media/nw0az1nj/q3-2026-results-announcement.pdf)


## Strong Specialty Medicines performance drives sales and core operating profit growth


-


Total Q3 sales £8.9 billion +4% AER; +5% CER


-


Specialty Medicines sales £3.9 billion (+15%); HIV sales £2.1 billion (+10%), Respiratory, Immunology & Inflammation £1.1 billion (+21%); Oncology £0.6 billion (+23%)


-


Vaccines sales £2.6 billion (-2%); *Shingrix* £0.8 billion (-5%); Meningitis vaccines £0.6 billion (+12%); and *Arexvy* £0.2 billion (-24%)


-


General Medicines sales £2.4 billion (stable); *Trelegy* £0.8 billion (+8%)


-


Total operating profit -16% and Total EPS -21% driven by Major restructuring charges of £328 million related to the Accelerate Growth programme and lower other net operating income, partly offset by Core operating profit growth


-


Core operating profit +5% and Core EPS +1% reflecting higher sales, favourable product and regional mix and higher royalty income, partly offset by increased investment in R&D and new asset launches and higher finance costs


-


Cash generated from operations of £3.1 billion with free cash flow of £2.1 billion

## Continued pipeline progress:


-


*Hibsago* approved in US and Japan, with data showing unprecedented functional cure rates and potential to redefine treatment of chronic hepatitis B


-


*Jemperli* approved in US as first immunotherapy for adults with dMMR/MSI-H locally advanced rectal cancer


-


Positive registrational data for *Jideytro* in first-line ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer (approved in US in second line in July)


-


Promising first global data for Ris-Rez in lung cancer; and positive phase I data for Mo-Rez in ovarian cancer


-


*Shingrix* pre-filled syringe approved in Japan, simplifying administration


-


mRNA seasonal influenza (flu) vaccine phase III trial initiated, following positive phase II data


-


On track to start 22 phase III trials in 2026 with 18 starts to date


## Growth outlooks:


-


2026 guidance reaffirmed with expected growth in: turnover 3% to 5%; Core OP 7% to 9%; Core EPS 7% to 9%


-


On track for 2031 sales outlook of more than £40 billion


-


Operating margin stable to improving through dolutegravir loss of exclusivity period of 2028-2030


## Shareholder returns:


-


Q3 2026 dividend of 17p declared; 70p expected for full year 2026


## Luke Miels, Chief Executive Officer, GSK:


“GSK has delivered another strong quarter, with our key growth drivers and new launches performing well. We remain focused on operational delivery, execution and accelerating R&D. Over recent months we have received 3 new specialty medicine approvals in the US: *Hibsago* , which has the potential to transform the treatment of chronic hepatitis B; *Jideytro* in non-small cell lung cancer; and *Jemperli* in rectal cancer. More broadly, in the late-stage portfolio, we are on track to start 22 phase III trials this year.”
